results.title: Attribution Windows: How to Set & Manage Them [Guide]
results.content: ## **What are Attribution Windows?**. An attribution window is the timeframe between a user’s interaction with your marketing touchpoints and their conversion. Attribution windows track interactions with your brand touchpoints (e.g., ads) and assign conversion credit within the window’s timeframe. If a customer clicks on an ad and makes a purchase within a 7-day attribution window, the ad gets credit for that conversion. For B2B companies with longer sales cycles, short attribution windows miss early touchpoints of the customer journey. Using each platform’s default attribution model and window:. * Facebook wouldn’t attribute the conversion on a 7-day window. Let’s say you’re running ads on Google Ads with a 30-day attribution window. * **Changing the attribution window disrupts reporting consistency.** Changing the attribution window alters how the platform counts conversions, so you won’t be able to compare your pre- and post-change data. If you need to change your attribution windows, do it between campaign phases (not mid-fight), annotate the change in your reporting tools, and run parallel tests (e.g., duplicate the campaign with different settings). Choosing the optimal attribution window should align with your business model, customer behavior, and campaign goals. With enough customer behavior data, you can use machine learning to identify the optimal attribution window for your business. Predictive modeling can also help balance attribution window length and conversion data by forecasting the real value you’ll capture (or miss) based on the window you choose. 5. Scroll to **Attribution Window Settings**. ## **Managing Attribution Windows for Multi-Touch and Cross-Channel Journeys**. Beyond attribution windows, the other key factor for measuring attribution is the model you use to assign conversion credit. Attribution windows help analyze future data, e.g., “If someone converts, who gets credit from the last ad they interacted with?”. In Attribution, you can customize the lookback window to adjust how many days to consider between an ad interaction and conversion. With Attribution, you access proprietary algorithms that combine actual customer data across platforms for more accurate multi-touch attribution compared to manual window setting. ### **How often should I reevaluate my attribution window settings?**. ### **Can I change my attribution window mid-campaign?**. ### **What’s the difference between click-through and view-through attribution windows?**.

results.title: java - clustered quartz instances schedule duplicate jobs? - Stack Overflow
results.content: # clustered quartz instances schedule duplicate jobs? I have a Tomcat web application A that schedules jobs with quartz framework. Recently we plan to move to JDBC Jobstore and set up a cluster, so that if one instance fails, the other instance will be able to run the job. My we application A will scan a business related database table and schedule quartz jobs during starting up and every 10 minutes afterwards. If I deploy two A applications on two different tomcat instances, then there will be two sets of duplicate jobs scheduled through Quartz. Do I need to extract the part of code that schedules jobs into a separate application and make sure only 1 instance is deployed so only 1 sets of jobs are scheduled? * if your quartz is in clustered mode, then there will be no duplication of jobs. You can make the task "scan a business related database table and schedule quartz jobs during starting up and every 10 minutes afterwards" itself a cron task in the clustered quartz instance. But then you will have multiple instances in the same cluster and they will try to schedule duplicate jobs, right? Clustered quartz scheduler setup is required when we want multiple instances of quartz and coordination between them so that only one instance executes the job. In this case, say suppose there are 4 nodes in the cluster, only one instance will be executing this scheduling cron task. How would a job scheduler like quartz work when you have multiple servers?
